newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria begins long funeral for first president.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria begins long funeral for first president.

text.p: Nigeria on Tuesday began a series of funeral ceremonies for its first president, Nnamdi Azikiwe, six months after he died.
Azikiwe, a champion of the struggle for African independence in the 1950s, died on May 11 and will be buried on Saturday, when he would have been 92 years old.

"Before then his body will lie in state in various places in the country to enable all Nigerians to pay their last respects to the fallen hero," said a spokesman for the government-appointed funeral planning committee.
The body on Tuesday was taken from the mortuary of Enugu teaching hospital in the east to Zungeru in the north where he was born in 1904.

It will be on display there and then move to Abuja, the federal capital, before being brought to Lagos and back to the east for burial in a ceremony billed as a mixture of Nigerian traditional rites and Christian religion.

"Zik of Africa", as he was widely known, was a titled chief in his native Iboland but was considered highly detribalised in a multi-ethnic nation which tribal tensions have frequently threatened to tear apart.
"Zik had a vision of a great Nigeria where all groups will live harmoniously," military ruler General Sani Abacha said in a eulogy at a symposium on the late president in Abuja on Monday.
"We must award him a dignifying and worthy rite of passage," he added.
It is as yet uncertain if any foreign dignitaries invited for the funeral will come to Nigeria, a nation being shunned for lack of democracy and alleged human rights abuses.
But officials said they expected Azikiwe's contemporaries in Africa like former President Julius Nyerere of Tanzania and former president Kenneth Kaunda of Zambia to attend.
Azikiwe became president in 1963 when it became a republic after independence from Britain in 1960. He remained until the first military coup in 1966.
